taxonomy.subtopic: Reduced oxygen content and impaired unloading despite normal arterial oxygen tension

questions.stem_html: Three family members develop headache, nausea, and confusion after using a gasoline-powered generator in an attached garage. One patient's arterial PO2 is 96 mm Hg, and a conventional pulse oximeter reads 99%, but lactate is increased. The accompanying oxygen-binding curves include the patient's curve. Which mechanism best explains the tissue hypoxia?

options.text_html: Carbon monoxide occupies hemoglobin binding sites and increases the oxygen affinity of remaining sites, reducing both oxygen content and unloading
Carbon monoxide lowers inspired oxygen tension, reducing dissolved oxygen in plasma without affecting hemoglobin
Carbon monoxide oxidizes ferrous iron to ferric iron, producing isolated methemoglobinemia
Carbon monoxide shifts the hemoglobin dissociation curve to the right by increasing 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate binding
Carbon monoxide selectively inhibits pulmonary diffusion, causing a markedly reduced arterial PO<sub>2</sub>

questions.explanation_html: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin with very high affinity, removing binding sites from oxygen transport. It also increases the affinity of the remaining oxygenated sites, shifting the dissociation relationship leftward and impairing tissue unloading. Arterial PO2 reflects dissolved oxygen and can remain normal, and conventional two-wavelength pulse oximetry can be misleading because it does not reliably distinguish oxyhemoglobin from carboxyhemoglobin.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: The principal problem is abnormal hemoglobin binding, not a reduction in inspired oxygen tension.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Methemoglobinemia involves oxidation of heme iron to the ferric state; carbon monoxide primarily forms carboxyhemoglobin.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Carbon monoxide shifts the effective dissociation relationship leftward, not rightward.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Arterial dissolved oxygen may remain normal because alveolar oxygen entry is not the primary defect.

questions.educational_objective: Carbon monoxide poisoning reduces oxygen-carrying capacity and impairs oxygen unloading while arterial PO2 may remain normal and conventional pulse oximetry may appear reassuring.
